div.p: ! At the Liverpool Assiaes, on Saturday, before Mr. Justice Grantham, Ward, 40, labourer, was indict ed for the manslaughter of William Foster, at ! Parr, on the 17th August. Mr. Swift and Mr. Steel prosecuted, and Mr. Seger WM far the defence. The ease for the proseamtion was that MI the date in question the priomer and the deeN4Seli were engaged in digging a trench at Baxter's Chemical Works, Parr. Thev quarrelied at a beerhouse :Le to who %WV the "bros. and half an hour afterwards the deceased's wife . met the prisoner and aiked him where her husband was. Ward replii-d that he was in the biorlioase. Mrs. Foster walked on a little further, and when she got ; nearer the works found her husband icing on the ground !dead, and with several wounds alma the head and face. !The prisoner seloomently made variousstatementm when !spoken to about the disci ivery, and before the he said he threw the deemised down and kicked him on the bead in self defence, as his own life NVa, in danger. Mr. Sept contended that the injuries sustaimsl by the deetWed were consistent with his having fallen upon something.—The prisoner was found guilty, and was sentenced to six mouths' imprisonment, with hard labour.
